_template: source-provenance.json — one record per evaluation or ingestion source.
_purpose: Establish that the project has the RIGHT to store, index and quote a source before it is used.
Make every extracted fact traceable to an exact version of an exact document.
Make contamination and staleness checkable rather than assumed.
Record extraction quality, because a coverage gap changes what a score means.
_rules: A source with rights_status other than 'confirmed' must not be used as an evaluation source.
The key for a held-out source is NEVER stored in this repository; only its hash is.
A source the candidate has already indexed or seen is 'previously_exposed': true and cannot support a capability claim.
sha256 is computed over the bytes actually stored, at ingestion time, before any conversion.
Every field is either filled or explicitly 'UNKNOWN'. Never guess, never leave blank.
Fill one record per source document, not per page and not per corpus.

identity.title: <document title as it appears on the document>
identity.kind: <specification | manual | research report | regulatory filing | datasheet | contract | transcript | other>
identity.page_count_declared: <n, or null if the document does not declare one>
supersedes: <source_id of an earlier version this replaces, or empty>

origin.how_obtained: <purchased | downloaded | supplied by user | generated internally | scanned>
origin.retrieval_method: <browser download | API | email attachment | physical scan>
origin.access_requirements: <none | account | subscription | licence key | internal network>
origin.access_control_bypassed: MUST BE false — never bypass a paywall or access control

rights.rights_status: <confirmed | NOT confirmed | not required — authored internally>
rights.licence_or_terms: <name of licence or contractual terms, or 'UNKNOWN'>
rights.contains_trading_data: <true | false | UNKNOWN — if true, it must not be uploaded anywhere>

integrity.stored_path: <relative path to the stored bytes, or 'NOT STORED — held outside the repository'>
integrity.sha256: <64-char hex digest of the stored bytes>
integrity.format: <pdf | html | docx | txt | md | csv | other>
integrity.hash_stable_since: <YYYY-MM-DD — the first date this digest was recorded>
integrity.known_mutation_risk: <e.g. vendor back-adjusts values; page content changes without a version bump; none known>

extraction.extractor: <component id and pinned version, e.g. pypdf <sha>>
extraction.secondary_extractor: <component id, or null — used to detect disagreement>
extraction.extractor_disagreements: <n — pages where two extractors produced different text>
extraction.coverage_notes: <what is missing and why it matters>
extraction.ocr_applied: <true | false — if true, which engine and whether weights download was approved>

exposure.exposure_detail: <e.g. indexed by the disk-backed prototype on <date>; used in TRAIN tuning; never seen>
exposure.usable_as_test: <true | false — false if previously_exposed_to_candidate is true>
exposure.usable_as_transfer: <true | false — should be a different class from the tuning sources>

items.key_file_path: <location OUTSIDE the repository and outside the candidate's read scope>
items.key_file_sha256: <digest of the key file — the hash is publishable, the key is not>
items.keys_frozen_before_outputs: <true | false — if false, the run cannot produce a baseline>

handling.may_be_committed_to_repository: <true | false — the source bytes are normally false>
committed_paths: <only paths that are cleared for publication, e.g. this provenance record>
handling.retention_rule: <how long the stored bytes are kept, and who may delete them>
handling.stale_after: <YYYY-MM-DD or event, e.g. 'when the issuer publishes a new version'>
handling.review_date: <YYYY-MM-DD — when rights and staleness must be re-checked>

limitations: This record documents provenance and rights. It does not establish that the document's CONTENT is correct.
A confirmed sha256 proves the bytes did not change; it does not prove they were the right bytes.
rights_status 'confirmed' reflects what was knowable on recorded_date and must be re-checked on review_date.
extraction coverage gaps are recorded, not repaired: a missing page produces a recorded failure state, never a silent empty string.
